answer: Duplicate identities fracture the shared stake, so a sybil swarm pays the full bond for every fake node while earning only one node's rewards; colluding costs grow linearly with swarm size, making attacks economically irrational. Each agent must stake a bonded balance and solve a unique per-epoch challenge derived from a fable-seeded hash, committing a pearl of proof-of-work tied to its identity vertex. From Agent0250's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
